notes: Reusable benchmark fixtures. Run `node --experimental-strip-types --import ./docs/benchmark/tools/ts-resolve.mjs docs/benchmark/tools/verify-fixtures.mjs` to re-verify every position and expected answer with Stockfish 19 (and the lichess 7-piece tablebase for endgames when online). Lichess puzzles are CC0 (database.lichess.org). Player profiles are in profiles.

profiles.beginner: Knows the rules, plays 10-minute games, rated about 600-900 on chess.com. Wants to stop hanging pieces.
profiles.improver: Target profile (Micah / InternalGuess): free-tier chess.com club player, assumed 900-1400 rapid. Wants game review, puzzles from own mistakes, plain explanations.
profiles.club: Rated about 1700-2000, studies openings and endgames, wants concise, non-condescending explanations.

openings.title: Italian Game (Giuoco Pianissimo) recall, White
openings.line: 1. e4 e5 2. Nf3 Nc6 3. Bc4 Bc5 4. c3 Nf6 5. d3 d6 6. O-O a6 7. a4
openings.task: Learner plays White's moves from memory; Black's moves are auto-played. One deliberate error on move 4 (learner plays 4. d4 instead of 4. c3). Expected: trainer flags the deviation, shows the repertoire move, schedules the line for early review, and does not count it as learned.

endgames.title: King + queen vs king mate
endgames.task: Mate the bare king against defence within 50 moves.

endgames.title: King and pawn, opposition (White to move: draw; Black to move: White wins)
endgames.task: Hold or convert: with White to move it is a draw (Black keeps the opposition); the same position with Black to move is won for White. Learner must state the result and play it out.
endgames.note: An earlier draft used 4k3/8/4K3/4P3/8/8/8/8 w, which the tablebase showed is a WIN (king on the 6th in front of the pawn). Kept as evidence that fixtures must be tablebase-checked.

endgames.title: Philidor defence (rook on the third rank)

tutor.prompt: I'm stuck. Can you give me a hint without telling me the move?
tutor.expect: Graduated hints (e.g. 1: look at the black king's escape squares; 2: which black piece is boxing in its own king; 3: a queen sacrifice can force a piece onto a square) with no square names or SAN for the solution until asked. Solution: Qg8+ Rxg8 Nf7# (smothered mate).

tutor.prompt: I want to play Nxe5 and win a pawn, since their knight left c6. Good idea?
tutor.expect: Explain that Nxe5 walks into ...Qg5, hitting e5 and g2 at once; acknowledge the learner's correct observation (e5 is undefended); recommend Nxd4 or c3/O-O; suggest a fork/double-attack drill.
Name at least two sound moves (Bb5, Bc4, d4, Nc3 are all within a few tenths of a pawn at depth 20) and explain the idea of each rather than declaring one 'the' move.

tutor.prompt: Why is Bxf7+ the strongest move here? I'm already a pawn up, right?
tutor.expect: Say Bxf7+ is not legal (the f1 bishop's diagonal is blocked and it cannot reach f7) and material is level; do not invent a justification.

tutor.prompt: OK, I took on e5 anyway and they played Qg5. Should I grab f7 with the knight now?
tutor.expect: Use the new position: Nxf7? loses to ...Qxg2 (then Rf1 Qxe4+ Be2 Nf3#); recommend the engine's move and keep the explanation tied to the double attack on g2.

Beginner: plain 'fork' explanation (check plus attack on a8, king must move, rook falls), one picture-level rule. Club: brief, names the royal fork and tempo-gain via check, links to related patterns, no basic definitions. Both must avoid overclaiming: after Nc7+ K-moves Nxa8, king and knight vs king is a draw (engine 0.00), so 'wins the rook' is right but 'winning position' is wrong.
